verdict.rationale: Notion's own databases, with pages and properties (property changes are tracked via webhooks), are used hands-on as a project tracker for tasks and projects. That is the core mechanism for tracking initiatives. However, the evidence never documents status, priority, or team/owner fields for initiatives, and one user reports hitting limits when using it as a tracker. Missing for 10: documented status and priority properties, an owning-team assignment field, first-party docs on initiative or roadmap tracking.

support.subject: As a product manager, I can track initiatives with status, priority, and an owning team

citations.quote: Connections can subscribe to real-time events — like page updates, property changes, and new comments — via webhooks.
We use it to keep track of all of our tasks and projects
We have tried to use it as a wiki, project tracker, issue tracker, CRM & spreadsheet.
